key_insight: At 12.5% La substitution in BaTiO3, enhanced electronic screening is linked to weaker ferroelectric polarization, lower static dielectric response, and reduced optical anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: Donor substitution offers a potential design lever for balancing ferroelectric, dielectric, and optical properties in perovskite oxide devices.
method: Density functional theory for structural, electronic, and optical properties.
Density-functional perturbation theory for phonons and dielectric response.
evidence_signal: Calculations indicate a dynamically stable doped structure with reduced Ti off-centering, hardened polar modes, reduced anomalous Born charges, and no mid-gap defect states.
watch_item: Results cover only 12.5% La substitution; broader doping trends and solar-cell performance are not established.
paper_title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
